fallback: This interactive lab needs JavaScript. A Kalman filter predicts depth and vertical velocity from known acceleration, then corrects that prediction using noisy depth fixes. The teal uncertainty band represents its assumed 95% interval, not a guarantee. The model and references below explain the method.
example:
See a simple exact example

Let h = 1 s, acceleration u = 0, Q = 0, R = 1 m², initial [depth, velocity] = [0, 0], and P = identity. Predicting gives P⁻ = [[2, 1], [1, 1]]. A fix z = 3 m gives gain [2/3, 1/3]. The corrected state is [2 m, 1 m/s] and P = [[2/3, 1/3], [1/3, 2/3]]. Depth moves two thirds of the way toward the fix.
